images.title: Where is the centre?
images.purpose: Pose the open question of where the centre of the upper arc of an eye must be, as a point equally far from X and Y.
images.composition: One eye outline centred in the frame with the segment XY through it; a single candidate centre point below XY, with plenty of white space around.
exact_structure: A horizontal grey (#6B7280) segment XY across the middle of the frame, about half the frame wide, with dark dots at X (left) and Y (right).
One teal (#0072B2) arc from X to Y bulging upwards: the upper arc of the eye.
One reddish purple (#CC79A7) dot well below the middle of XY, the guessed centre of the upper arc, with a reddish purple question mark beside it.
Two thin dashed grey (#6B7280) segments, one from the dot to X and one from the dot to Y, each carrying one small tick mark to show they are equal.
No lower arc, no other points, no compass drawn.
One short caption line at the bottom of the frame.
labels: Same distance from X and Y?
rejection: the reddish purple dot drawn above XY instead of below it
the two dashed segments carrying different numbers of tick marks, or more than one candidate centre shown
a lower arc or a finished second centre drawn, which would answer the question
images.takeaway: The centre of an arc through both X and Y must be the same distance from X as from Y.
images.description: An upper eye arc from X to Y, with a guessed centre below XY joined to X and Y by two equal dashed lines and a question mark.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video for this concept.
images.teaching_notes: Ask students to say why the two dashed lines must be equal before the next topic finds the centre exactly.

image_decisions.why: A single guessed centre with two equal distances makes the question to keep in mind concrete.
